description: dnslookup: simple command-line DNS lookup tool that supports every DNS protocol: plain DNS over UDP and TCP, DNS-over-TLS, DNS-over-HTTPS (HTTP/2 and HTTP/3), DNS-over-QUIC and DNSCrypt.
notes: Command: dnslookup <name> [server]. The 'dnslookup' shortcut in Scoop Apps shows examples and waits for a key.
The protocol comes from the server address: 9.9.9.9, tcp://, tls://, https://, h3://, quic://, sdns://.
Options are environment variables, not flags. In cmd: SET RRTYPE=AAAA (stays set in that window until SET RRTYPE=).
In PowerShell: $env:RRTYPE = 'AAAA' (until Remove-Item Env:RRTYPE). Others: JSON=1, VERBOSE=1, DNSSEC=1, CLASS=CH, SUBNET=1.2.3.4/24.
Only one of gesu/dnslookup and main/dnslookup can be installed: Scoop treats them as the same app.

script: # dnslookup.exe prints its usage and exits at once, so the 'dnslookup' shortcut opens this micro-launcher instead.
':: dnslookup: shows what dnslookup does and how to run it, then waits for a key.',
':: Written by the gesu Scoop bucket at install time.',
'ECHO dnslookup sends one DNS query over the protocol you pick and prints the answer.',
'ECHO Run it from any console as dnslookup.',
'ECHO The server address picks the protocol:',
'ECHO       The same, connecting to 1.1.1.1 without resolving the server name first',
'ECHO Options are environment variables, not flags. In cmd:',
'ECHO Others: JSON=1, VERBOSE=1, DNSSEC=1, CLASS=CH, SUBNET=1.2.3.4/24, PAD=1, VERIFY=0',
